problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -6 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & 4 & -1 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

feedback.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 & -6 & -3 \\ 0 & -4 & 12 & 36 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
feedback.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 & -6 & -3 \\ 0 & -4 & 12 & 36 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -4 & 12 & 36 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -4 & 12 & 36 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -9 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-y+2z=1 \\  & y-3z=-9 \\  & z=1,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $z=1$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
y-3(1)=-9\,⟹\,y=-6.
$$

Finally, substituting both $y=-6$ and $z=1$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x-(-6)+2(1)=1\,⟹\,x=-7.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-7,y=-6$, and $z=1.$ Or, in vector form, $⟨-7,-6,1⟩.$
